assessment.nobel_worthiness: Flocking is the paradigm of non-equilibrium collective order: a continuous symmetry can be spontaneously broken in two dimensions once the dynamics is out of equilibrium, which evades the Mermin-Wagner constraint. The hydrodynamic theory gives anomalous fluctuations and scaling that equilibrium statistical mechanics cannot produce, and the work founded the field of active matter, with reach into biology, robotics and materials. As a complex-systems theorist I regard it as original, clear and conceptually deep.
assessment.attribution: The Vicsek model (numerical, minimal alignment rule) and the Toner-Tu hydrodynamic theory (analytical, symmetry-based) are distinct and complementary decisive contributions. The three supplied names cover both strands; Toner and Tu share the continuum theory and Vicsek the minimal model. Priority questions between early related work (e.g. on alignment dynamics) are not resolved by the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: The theory is nearly three decades old and extremely widely adopted. Direct quantitative confirmation of the specific Toner-Tu exponents is thinner than the qualitative confirmation in bird, fish, bacterial and colloidal systems; recent simulations and experiments support the picture but some exponent details are still debated. Recognition would be timely rather than premature.
uncertainties: Quantitative experimental confirmation of the predicted exponents in real systems is incomplete.
Whether the prize should reward the minimal model, the hydrodynamic theory, or both, and how to treat other early contributors, is not settled by the supplied credit.
I am recalling the exponent and experimental status from memory and have not verified it here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The KPZ equation defines a universality class for non-equilibrium interface growth and stochastic dynamics, tied to random matrices, directed polymers, exclusion processes and integrable probability. The exact Tracy-Widom-type fluctuation statistics and their unexpected appearance in many settings make this one of the cleanest bridges between statistical physics and mathematics. It is very close to my own interests in stochastic processes and random matrices.
assessment.attribution: Kardar and Zhang are the originators of the equation together with Parisi, whose name is not in the supplied credit and who is already a laureate for other work; this leaves a real allocation problem. Takeuchi's liquid-crystal turbulence experiments gave the first clean confirmation of the universal distributions. Kardar, Zhang and Takeuchi is a defensible configuration from the supplied names. The mathematical exact solutions are not represented among the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Theory dates from 1986. Experimental confirmation came in 2010 with further tests in several systems, including recent spin-chain and cold-atom realisations, so the interpretation is stable and independently supported. The timing is mature.
uncertainties: Omission of Parisi from the supplied credit complicates a fair prize configuration.
Exact solutions by mathematicians and the experiment together form a compound discovery whose parts may merit different recognition.
Details of the later spin-chain and cold-atom confirmations are recalled from memory rather than verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The jamming picture unifies the rigidity of granular matter, foams, emulsions and glasses through a critical point with scaling, an isostatic coordination number and anomalous vibrational modes. It addresses disordered solids, a hard problem for statistical physics, with a simple and testable framework. Importance is high for soft and disordered matter; reach beyond that community is narrower than for the top choices.
assessment.attribution: Liu and Nagel are the clear originators of the 1998 jamming phase diagram and subsequent development; the two-person credit is clean. Contributions by others on isostaticity, marginal stability and the mean-field theory of the jamming of hard spheres are important but not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of simulation and experiment, including colloidal and granular systems, support the scaling picture. The relation between jamming and the glass transition remains actively debated, so the central idea is mature but not all of its consequences are closed.
uncertainties: Boundary between the jamming critical point and the glass transition is unsettled.
Exact universality class and the role of finite-size and protocol dependence remain debated.
Contributions of mean-field and replica-theory work may be undercredited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realised controllable Hubbard-type models, with the superfluid to Mott-insulator transition as the landmark, and opened a route to quantum simulation of strongly correlated matter. The conceptual and experimental impact on many-body physics is large, and it links directly to statistical-mechanics questions about phases and dynamics.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with collaborators such as Jaksch, who is not in the supplied credit) proposed the Bose-Hubbard realisation; Greiner and Bloch performed the 2002 Mott-insulator experiment, and Bloch led later developments. The three names support a theory-plus-experiment configuration, but other contributors to the proposal and to related early experiments are not named. Overlap with other candidates crediting Zoller and Bloch makes the exact framing uncertain.
assessment.maturity: The field is mature and widely replicated, with quantum-gas microscopes and applications to magnetism, though practical quantum advantage in simulation is still being demonstrated. Recognition would be timely.
uncertainties: Credit for the original proposal is shared with persons outside the supplied names.
Overlap with other candidates (lattice simulation, Rydberg arrays, trapped-ion theory) leaves the best bounded discovery unclear.
Extent to which simulators answer open condensed-matter questions is still evolving.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators introduced a new classification of band insulators, with protected edge and surface states, and shifted the way condensed matter is organised around topology. The work is original, clear and has had a deep, lasting influence on materials physics and beyond.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele proposed the Z2 invariant and the spin Hall state in graphene; Molenkamp's group made the first experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells, following the theory of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, who are not credited here (Zhang is deceased). This leaves a real allocation question. The three supplied names are defensible but not complete.
assessment.maturity: Extensively confirmed in many materials and by ARPES, transport and other tools. Maturity is high and recognition would be timely, though the importance of the topology theme is already partly recognised by the 2016 prize.
uncertainties: Missing credit for the HgTe theory proposal and three-dimensional topological insulator contributors.
Partial overlap in theme with the 2016 prize on topological phase transitions.
Several names are outside the supplied credit, so the fairest configuration cannot be verified from this list alone.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory is exact in infinite dimensions and turned the Hubbard-model Mott transition and correlated-metal problems into a tractable quantum-impurity problem. It is the workhorse for correlated materials, combined with electronic-structure methods. It is a statistical-physics idea of broad computational and conceptual importance.
assessment.attribution: Metzner and Vollhardt introduced the infinite-dimension limit in 1989; Georges and Kotliar, with Kotliar's collaborators, formulated the DMFT mapping in 1992. Metzner is not in the supplied credit; the three supplied names are a credible configuration but the allocation is not fully clean.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with a long record of applications and cross-checks against experiment; however, its systematic accuracy for finite-dimensional systems (cluster extensions) is still being examined.
uncertainties: Credit for Metzner and other early contributors is absent from the supplied names.
Direct experimental confirmation is indirect, through materials-specific calculations.
Whether the discovery is a physical phenomenon or a computational method may weigh on recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics created strong coherent coupling between superconducting qubits and microwave resonators, and is the backbone of superconducting quantum processors and quantum-limited readout. The impact on quantum technology and fundamental tests is substantial and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Blais and collaborators proposed the architecture in 2004; Wallraff, Schoelkopf and co-authors demonstrated strong coupling the same year. The supplied names split theory and experiment sensibly. The Yale and Zurich experimental groups are both credited, but other early contributors are not.
assessment.maturity: Very mature and independently reproduced, though the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits is closely related and may make recognition feel too close or overlapping.
uncertainties: Overlap with the recent 2025 prize on superconducting circuits.
The weight of theoretical versus experimental credit in 2004 work.
Outside my own expertise, so my judgement of relative priority is less secure.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Conformal field theory of two-dimensional critical phenomena gave exact critical exponents and operator content for a large class of statistical models, and underlies much of modern field theory and string theory. It is conceptually central to critical phenomena and the renormalisation-group picture I work with.
assessment.attribution: The 1984 Belavin-Polyakov-Zamolodchikov paper is the decisive contribution; the three supplied names are a clean configuration. Related contributions by others, for example on the Virasoro algebra and unitary minimal models, are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature and thoroughly confirmed, including numerical verification in lattice models and by experiment. The question is whether an old theoretical discovery is still best recognised now, and whether its physical rather than mathematical content is the decisive part.
uncertainties: Much of the work is mathematical physics; the experimental connection is indirect.
Time since discovery and the question of whether recognition is overdue or already absorbed by other prizes.
Relative credit for other early contributors cannot be resolved here.
